title: Classification
description: What each story in a Feature Inventory costs to build, keyed by its feature id. Separate from the inventory on purpose: the inventory records what the source says, and this records the judgements the cost model prices on. An extraction skill that also assigned these was deciding what things cost, and a re-extraction could silently revert a human's correction. Now a re-extraction cannot touch a judgement at all — it can only orphan one, which classification-merge.py reports rather than drops. Written by est-estimate; every axis maps to a coefficient family in cost-model.json.

inventory.description: Path of the Feature Inventory these judgements were made against. The join is by feature id, so a classification pointed at a different inventory is a silent mis-pricing waiting to happen.

cost_model.description: Path of the cost model whose bands and exemplars the classifier read. A band table means nothing without the exemplars it was calibrated with.

how.description: Whether the pass ran fanned out across subagents or sequentially, and whether a reconciliation pass ran. A reader comparing two classifications needs to know which way each was produced.

seed.description: The feature ids classified first, as this run's own reference class. Every classifier was given these, so they are the thing to re-read when the bands look inconsistent across epics.

features.description: Keyed by feature id — F* for extracted, I* for implicit scope. Standing work (SW-*) is not here: est-estimate synthesises its tags from the cost model's standing_work catalogue, because it is the same on every project.

compressibility.description: How much BMad compresses building this

review_tier.description: routine / sensitive / critical human review burden

clarity.description: How precisely the source specifies it

novelty.description: standard or novel relative to work the team has done before

why.description: One line, about THIS story. A tag without a reason is a black box coefficient, which this module does not ship.

status.description: inferred: set by a classification pass. confirmed: a human agreed. overridden: a human changed it. unclassified: the shape is known and the judgement is deliberately absent — a recovered anchor project, which must be classified before it can be priced. Re-classification must never downgrade confirmed or overridden back to inferred.

triggers.description: For review_tier: the source phrases that raised the tier, quoted.
